_meta.usage: DDD alone or a whole number: 21, (21) 2541-1234, (21) 98765-4321, (0xx21) 2541-1234, 021 2541-1234, +55 21 2541-1234 (keys 0DD, and 055DD for the +55 form). A landline has 8 digits starting 2–5 and a mobile 9 starting 9; for an old 8-digit mobile (6xxx- to 9xxx-xxxx, before 2016) pass the DDD alone. A carrier code between the 0 and the DDD (0 15 11 …), a number without its DDD and 0800/0300/4004-xxxx numbers don't fit this table and are not looked up. Without --country, (21) … also matches Shanghai and İstanbul codes and (55) … Chinese and Korean ones: pass --country br when the country is known
_meta.note: 67 DDDs (Anatel 'código nacional', CN). Each match is a state with the municipalities the code covers (count, largest by 2022 census population); four codes cross a state line: 61 (Distrito Federal and 12 municipalities of Goiás), 42 (Porto União, SC), 47 (Rio Negro, PR) and 49 (Barracão, PR). Anatel's file lacks six municipalities: Aroeiras do Itaim and Nazária (Piauí), Figueirão (Mato Grosso do Sul, which has one code, so it is counted there), Ipiranga do Norte, Itanhangá and Boa Esperança do Norte (Mato Grosso); the rows say so. The 2019 file was checked in November 2026 against the current numbers of 26 town halls (border towns and the DF's surroundings) with no change found; Anatel's panel with the current plan was down for maintenance on the fetch date. Since Anatel's 2026 reform every fixed line in a DDD area is in one local area, so a landline places a business somewhere in the DDD area, no closer. A mobile number keeps the DDD where it was registered (portability stays within the DDD), but a phone can be used anywhere.
